messages:
alex_r: Kepler Health asked for a short technical trial focused on three user journeys. They want clear success criteria and a simple SOW. Can we sketch this out here?

mona_v: From our discovery: 1) clinical triage (flag urgent cases + short structured rationale), 2) post-visit note draft (from dictation + vitals), 3) patient-facing FAQ chat (PHI-safe). They emphasized EU data residency.

diego_t: Clarify streaming needs: triage should feel interactive (streaming tokens ok), note draft can be async batch. That will affect model choices and cost.

alex_r: Good. Propose endpoints: /v1/kepler/triage (stream), /v1/kepler/note (sync), /v1/kepler/patient-chat (chat, no PHI persisted). @riley_h can you confirm hosting options?

riley_h: Hosting note: because of customer-managed keys ask, Dedicated with customer KMS or Private will be required if they insist on HSM. Otherwise we can run EU-hosted hosted API with strict logging. I recommend Dedicated for the POC to reduce friction.

secbot: Security checklist posted: SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 pending; requirement: console MFA, SSO (SAML), VPC peering for audit logs, and option to redact request bodies from logs.

mona_v: Success criteria suggested by Kepler on call: triage precision >= 0.88 on their benchmark, clinician note quality >= 4/5 avg from 10 clinicians, p95 latency for triage < 600ms. They asked for a transparent eval process.

diego_t: For evals, ask them for 60 labeled examples per journey (min); we'll run our harness and compare vs their baseline. Proposal for pass/fail: triage recall >= 0.82 and precision >= 0.88 OR after two tuning iterations, otherwise trial considered inconclusive.

alex_r: Pricing question: they want predictable trial cost with a 750k token cap. I'll propose a flat trial fee that includes up to 750k tokens and one tuning cycle, with a published overage rate. Any pushback?

riley_h: Sounds fine. Capacity notes: assume peak 30 qps for triage, average payload 180 tokens. Recommend 2 gpus in dedicated pool for safety. I'll prepare cost delta hosted vs dedicated.

mona_v: Endpoint examples I'll drop here for the SOW. Sample triage payload:
```
POST /v1/kepler/triage
{
  "conversation": "Patient: I've had chest pain... Clinician: ...",
  "vitals": {"hr": 110, "bp": "140/90"},
  "stream": true
}
```

diego_t: Model plan: low-latency quantized variant for triage, higher-capacity for notes. Include a fallback policy: on high latency or errors, route triage to best-effort summary (degraded but still functional). We'll include logging of fallback events in dashboard.

secbot: They also asked for deletion SLA: delete customer data on request within 48 hours and option to disable request logging. Add to SOW. Also note: legal will review HSM requirement (could push to Private).

alex_r: Timeline draft: Day 0 sign SOW & data share, Day 3 infra ready + model config, Day 5 run 1 with eval set, Day 10 handover + report. We should be explicit about who provides labeled evals and when.

mona_v: Action items: 1) diego prepare eval harness + prompt templates; 2) riley provide capacity + cost numbers; 3) secbot/infosec to detail controls and HSM implications; 4) alex draft SOW + trial pricing.

infra-bot: provisioning: creating dedicated-poc-eu (id: ded-kepler-042).

riley_h: I've uploaded a cost workbook and a short runbook for switching to Private if HSM is mandated: https://drive.redwood/kepler/poc/runbook.xlsx

diego_t: Eval harness link: https://ci.redwood/kepler/harness (contains scripts, metrics calc, and sample prompt pairs). I'll include rubric for clinician ratings.

mona_v: I'll assemble the SOW endpoints matrix and include explicit pass/fail thresholds and the 2-week retune allowance.

alex_r: I'll send this consolidated SOW to Kepler and ask for their eval bundles by EOD Wed. Reply here once you've uploaded your artifacts.

secbot: Reminder: include clause that logs cannot contain full patient identifiers and that audit logs can be redacted on request.

alex_r: Great work team. Will follow up after Kepler responds. :+1:
